source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Kenji,

The latest iteration is moving the hierarchy back toward the right direction, so thank you. To prevent further backward steps, however, I think the review process now needs to be reset and standardized.

Going forward, every presentation should use the same format. For each option in every future iteration, please provide two versions using this comparison layout:

Left column

Hero V peak height
Alphabet cap height
Second V peak height

Right column

Show the identical artwork again, but remove every reference line.

This format lets me assess the design itself and verify separately that the hierarchy remains intact.

Unless I explicitly ask for a change, the following relationships must stay locked:

Hero V — Keep the currently agreed hierarchy and the established percentage of elevation for the right arm. This is still the system’s master geometry.

Second V — Derive it proportionally from the Hero V while preserving the agreed relationship above the cap height of the surrounding letters. It must read as a quiet echo of the Hero V and never compete with it.

É Accent — Copy the Hero V’s right arm exactly, end it at the identical peak height, and carry over precisely the same terminal geometry.

New Assignment: Terminal Exploration

Because the hierarchy is now close enough, the next exploration should focus exclusively on terminal language. Keep every other element identical and develop six distinctly different terminal treatments for the Hero V only.

These should not be six refinements of one solution. I want genuinely distinct design philosophies. The following five directions may help guide the work:

1\. Soft Architectural

Draw from carved limestone, travertine, and high-end architecture.

Retain geometric construction
Ease the corners subtly
Create warmth without appearing rounded
Convey quiet confidence

2\. Sculpted

Treat the termination as though it was not cut, but carefully sculpted instead.

Use subtle transitions
Make the refinement almost invisible
Feel hand-finished rather than manufactured
Maintain elegant restraint

3\. Faceted Gemstone

Approach it like a precision-cut gemstone.

Introduce multiple subtle planes
Keep it refined rather than sharp
Make it luxurious without becoming decorative
Keep the result crisp, yet polished

4\. Cast Bronze

Imagine molten bronze being poured into a mold.

Preserve precise geometry
Allow the casting process to soften the edges naturally
Make it less mechanical
Give it a timeless, enduring quality

5\. Bespoke Furniture

Reference museum-quality cabinetry and artisan furniture making.

Break the edge intentionally
Keep it engineered without ever becoming harsh
Express sophisticated craftsmanship
Suggest understated luxury

6\. Your Interpretation

Please also create one concept based entirely on your own interpretation. Drawing on everything we have developed together during the past several weeks, follow your design intuition and surprise me with the solution you believe captures the VEILLVÉ identity most successfully.

The objective is not simply a softer vector; it is a different material quality. Rather than reading as the end of a line, the terminal should resemble the edge treatment of an heirloom object.

It should feel:

Architectural
Refined
Quiet
Luxurious
Timeless
Precision-crafted

It should never feel:

Calligraphic
Rounded
Decorative
Fashion-oriented
Aggressive or sharp

After we identify the correct terminal language for the Hero V, apply it directly to the É accent and proportionally to the second V.

Thank you.

The established hierarchy, kerning, baseline, and overall composition remain locked; the source changes terminal exploration and derivation rather than the composition requirement.
The terminal material metaphors concern edge geometry and terminal language, not the selected champagne-gold finish or its distribution.
The terminal concepts operationalize existing brand qualities but do not change the broader Veillvé positioning or expression requirements.
The decision does not alter the wordmark-led identity or the prohibition on requiring a separate icon or monogram.
The terminal derivation and exploration decision does not change the production-ready asset-delivery obligation.
